utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: In this case, as well, I took along all the representatives of the foreign media who were in the area of Pristina then and who wanted to go and see Junik and see for themselves what it was that had happened there, because the Albanians had informed them that Junik had been razed to the ground, that everything had been torched and destroyed. I took them to the actual site; and at the very entrance into Junik, we found kilometres-long trenches, bunkers, obstacles on the road, and the like. All of this had been placed there previously; but through a terrorist action that had been carried out just before that, all of this was removed and traffic of goods and people was unhindered at that point. We could see that there was some minor damage on the facades of buildings; however, the reports made by some people were absolutely untrue. So that was my objective, that was my task. At the moment when I was spokesperson, I wanted to inform foreign journalists in a timely and truthful manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What did you say on this occasion, do you remember?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: I said that the Ministry of the Interior will continue to act towards the terrorist gangs as we did before that, that we would ensure peaceful life for all citizens, irrespective of ethnic affiliation and that normal conditions would be created for living and working there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like us to move on to disciplinary responsibility and misdemeanours and crimes committed by policemen. What about proceedings concerning such offences, under who is this in the police?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: Disciplinary and criminal proceedings against employees of the ministry is within the domain of the work of the chief of a particular secretariat. Should I explain?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a moment. Before we continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have in e-court 6D464, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think that you have this in the binder before you. Could you please tell me how are misdemeanour proceedings instituted, for instance.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: This is a dispatch of Bosko Petric, chief of the secretariat in Pristina, that he sends to the Ministry of the Interior, to the police administration, since the person involved is a policeman who had committed a traffic misdemeanour. In this dispatch, he is asking for consent to file a misdemeanour report. Secretariats sought such approval or consent from the appropriate administrations within the ministry in cases when criminal reports were filed and misdemeanour reports and when employees were supposed to be removed from the ministry on account of the nature of the violation of work duties on a temporary basis. There was no problem regarding this kind of consent or approval from the appropriate administration, but sometimes this was sought because the ministry compiled a review concerning all employees of the Ministry of the Interior in terms of misdemeanours, crimes, and disciplinary infractions. Every three months these reviews were sent to the secretariats for the sake of their own information so that they would know what was going on among the employees in the ministry in terms of violations of work duty and irresponsible conduct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know in practice whether sometimes consent was not given to initiate criminal or misdemeanour proceedings?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: That never happened. It is only natural that if any citizen, let alone a policeman, commits a crime that proceedings should be instituted in accordance with the law.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No to dwell on this question too long, for the transcript, I'm just going to spell out the documents that deal with this; that is, 6D1339, 6D1340, 6D1343, 6D1344, 6D1345, 6D1346, 6D1348, 6D1349, and 6D1357.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I just indicate ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes. May I just indicate that most of these documents were notified to us sometime yesterday afternoon in contravention of the Court order as to notification, and most of these documents are not translated. And I do not believe that reading out these exhibit numbers can in any way assist or can be a basis of these documents being received in evidence. Those are the three matters I would like to bring to the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, first of all, I think none of these are translated; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Give me one second, please. The document we are -- just showed to the witness is translated, and that's why I was using only that -- that one. The others are basically the same and they are not translated yet, and we informed the Prosecutors two or three days ago. But I'm not using that, just for the reference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, you've been advised that or, well, we have been advised that you notified the Prosecutor yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We notified him two days ago, on the -- a day and a half --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's 12.30 a.m. on the 6th of March.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Obviously before Mr. Stamp would go to his bed? So why so late?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the conversation with this witness, we discovered that these documents explained the same subjects, so we keep our witnesses until 2.00 a.m. every day, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And they're all similar letters --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- to the ministry seeking approval for misdemeanour --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, all the same subjects, all the same letters. It's almost all the same as before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, we are not prepared to even allow these documents to be marked for identification. We will refuse any form of admission of these documents. If you can provide a basis later to have them admitted from the bar table, that's another matter, but we would obviously bear in mind at that stage that the Prosecution did not have an opportunity to cross-examine the witness through whom these were sought to be presented. So let's move on to something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just about this document, 6D464, where approval is sought to submit a misdemeanour report, I'd like to ask you: Did the MUP staff have any role in deciding on issues of misdemeanour, liability, where members of the ministry were concerned in Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: The MUP staff did not and could not have any role in deciding whether our employees would be called to responsibility or not, because it's all regulated by the Law on the Police Force and Law on Disciplinary Proceedings when disciplinary infractions are concerned, and when misdemeanour and crime is concerned, all the same rules apply as for civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did the MUP staff have any role in proceedings or giving approval to file a criminal report against a member of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: No, it did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did the MUP staff have any role to play in disciplinary proceedings against members of the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: It did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Was a copy of this sent to the MUP staff?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at 6D464.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: It was not. It was only sent to the Ministry of the Interior of Serbia, the police administration, and the chief in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us something about the procedure for adopting work-plans in the secretariat of internal affairs and its internal organizational units?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Meanwhile, I would like to call up P1074.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's in your binder. Can you find it, P1074?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: The number again?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: P1074. Could you open page 2, para 1.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: I haven't found it yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Look in the back.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: Yes, I found it, 1074.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Tell us, first, do you see what this document is?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: It's the annual work-plan for the SUP of Pristina for 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you turn to the next page, para 1, and tell us something about the procedures for adopting work-plans in the secretariat of the interior and its internal organizational units.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: Annual plans, annual work-plans for the secretariat of internal affairs, were adopted based on the annual work-plan of the public security sector of the Ministry of the Interior, and these work-plans were submitted to secretariats towards the end of the current year so that they could make their own annual plan for the next year. Work-plans were made at the secretariat by lines of work and by area, then they were aggregated at the level of the secretariat, and then they would be submitted to the administration for information and analysis at the ministry in three copies, two of them bound. They were then reviewed; and if it was judged by the administrations for particular lines of work that there was certain omissions or deficiencies in these drafts, that something should be added, the secretariats were informed accordingly to make these additions and corrections and that they should submit a corrected version to be adopted. After they were adopted at the level of the ministry, they would be implemented primarily through monthly plans that were drafted subsequently and submitted again to the administration for information and analysis at the ministry, one by one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: From this first paragraph, what is defined as the focus in the work of the secretariat for 1999?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: Combatting crime and maintaining public order and law in the area of the secretariat.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In e-court, we have wrong pages. We need pages number 2 but we'll be moving from this page anyways.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to ask you to open page 11 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's page 14 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which part of the plan do we see at the beginning of page 11 in B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: Combatting homicides and sexual offences and crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is specified?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: In para 1, crimes of terrorism committed in the previous year.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In item 2 -- or rather, number 2?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: Number 2 is solving the crime of murder committed by unidentified perpetrator or perpetrators. On the 2nd of December, 1998, against Ilir Durmisi, against Afrim Malici from Donja Dubnica, and Tal Hizri from Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Once criminal reports were filed involving an unidentified perpetrator, would these cases still be worked on although the perpetrator was not identified?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: Yes. Work would continue until the perpetrator is found, and we see that this work is continuing in the next year regardless of who the victim is, and we see from this one that the victims are Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And number 3?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: It's solving the crime of rape -- attempted rape, rather, committed in March 1998 against Novka Zujovic from Bijelo Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The perpetrator is identified in this one?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: No, he's not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The victim is identified?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: Correct, the perpetrator is not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Crimes of rape like crimes of homicide, were they still processed although the perpetrator was not identified?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: Of course, all measures were taken to identify the perpetrator.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, please turn to page 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That will be page 15 in English, under number 2. We'll need page 16 in English, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Under number 2, what do we read?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: You mean page 12?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: In this item, measures are planned that need to be effectively taken to combat and elucidate the most serious crimes, armed conflicts, and settlements of accounts among criminals, looting and republic, extortion, blackmail, kidnapping, aggravated theft by burglaring cash registers, apartments, post offices, petrol stations, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But we also had terrorism, homicide, and rape on the previous page. What is the dead-line?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: It is a permanent task. It was a permanent task until the cases were elucidated.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us now go back to page 11, please, the last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it is page 14 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please read out the last paragraph on page 11, which carries over to page 12.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: "With the members of the police, ambushes will be organized, blockades and raids in the area of Pristina where there are crimes committed in terms of property crime in the locations they occur most frequently, in particular in the settlements of Daradnija, Ulpijana, Suncani Breg, Vranjavac, and Dragodan, in order to prevent any further crimes from being committed and in an attempt to apprehend the perpetrators thereof on site."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please explain.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: By analysing these security events, in this case crimes in the territory of that town and the secretariat, in the previous year, it was established that these crimes were most frequently committed in the settlements mentioned in the plan. That's why the plan foresees that in order to prevent any such crimes to be committed in the next year in the aforementioned settlements, ambushes and raids be organized by police members. This should have been preventive action and also an attempt to catch as many perpetrators as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Why were these settlements characteristic or typical?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: They were also notorious for the activity of terrorist gang members as well as concerning attacks on state officials, Vranjevac in particular.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The same page, 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]In the English, I believe it is 16.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There is item 4 there. What is the focus of that item of the work-plan?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: The focus is to continue undertaking measures and activities to prevent eruption of inter-ethnic conflicts and disturbances of public law and order in neighbourhoods with mixed ethnic population, as well as to ensure effective protection of personal security of citizens.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Item 5, what can we see there? What was the focus when controlling vehicles?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: The focus was to identify perpetrators who illegally attempt to introduce all types of fire-arms into the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 13, please. It is 17 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is the goal of item 1 of page 13?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: The aim was to solve the crimes of armed robbery and robbery with violence in retaining stolen goods. We have the victims, Ivica Jovanovic from Pristina, Ljuljzim Musa from Urosevac, and Ahmet Kurtoli from Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was their ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: One is Serbian, two are Albanian. Ivica Jovanovic is a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we see whether any activities were taken up to that point?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: Yes. Through operative work and contacts in the field, information gathering commenced; also by using the secretary files, MOS to try and identify the perpetrators.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We have some figures there beginning with "KU." What does it mean?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: It is the crime register and the year when the criminal report was submitted to the competent prosecutor's office; for example, 1679/98.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Page -- excuse me, the same page, item 2, what do we see there?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: What is planned is further operative work, that is, for the next year, concerning the cases of impersonating an officer, whereby crimes were committed. During the previous year, there were one, two, three, four -- seven criminal reports submitted for the crimes committed by people impersonating officers by probably wearing certain pieces of uniform. What is also requested is further operative work to resolve these cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Item 3, we see there that there were aggravated thefts occurring in peacetime as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to go to page 18.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We see the title number 2, page 24 in English, activities pertaining to public order and law and other police tasks?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I've already said that it is page 18 in the Serbian version, bullet point 3. What is planned?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: Item 3, what is planned is to maintain stable public law and order and to prevent inter-ethnic conflicts as well as all aspects of hostile activity. What is envisaged is also an attempt to try to prevent any revival of terrorist activities of Albanian separatists, as well as to oppose any attempts aimed at deterioration of security situation in the area of the secretariat.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]I apologise. It seems that in the English version the title was on another page, page 25.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, page 21, please, professional education and lawfulness, item 1. Can we see there who put together the programme of professional training or education?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: The programme of professional education or training of authorised officials.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] it is page 29 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please go on.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: The programme of professional training of authorised officials, that is put into place by the sector of public security of the Ministry of the Interior of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is there a system of permanent professional training in the police?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. It existed then and it exists now. There is a system of permanent professional training and education in place.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Page 22, please, item 3. The second paragraph of item 3, what is planned therein?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: It is planned that there should be regular control of the legality and quality of methods used by police stations and policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What about item 4, what is it about?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: It is about stopping the abuse and overstepping authority and other forms of illegal and deviant behaviour by policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What about item 5 --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is item 5 about?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: It foresees the obligation to continue taking all measures and actions in the jurisdiction of the ministry, in order to consistently implement the agreement reached between the president of the FRY and the Special US Envoy concerning the arrival of the OSCE verification mission in Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As for the second paragraph of item 5, what does it say?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: It mentions energetic efforts to prevent the implementation of any further plans of Albanian terrorists and planting explosive devices along roads, communications, sport, and economic facilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]Page 26, please, in the Serbian and 36 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we see from this item who conducts the training of PJP and following what programme?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: The training of the PJP is implemented according to the plan of the MUP of Serbia, as can be seen from the several items of the secretariat plan. What is foreseen is the training of the PJP and reserve policemen within the framework of the companies that exist in the secretariat.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In practice, did the secretariat of the internal affairs in Pristina have to include a programme of training for the members of its companies?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]Page 31 in the Serbian, please. It is page 43 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Item 1, what is foreseen there? What should take place?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it foreseen in this item that there might be an increase in terrorist activities?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: What item exactly?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Defence --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Preparation of defence.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: Since Albanian terrorists are active in order to try and accomplish ethnic cleansing --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the witness please slow down when reading. The interpreter did not locate that passage in the English version. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Filic, the interpreter could not translate everything that you read there because you read it rather quickly. Could you read that again, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. This is the area of defence preparations. It is stated as follows: "In view of the activities of Albanian terrorist gangs whose goals are ethnic cleansing and secession from Serbia as well as creating an independent state of Kosovo, defence preparation tasks must be organized in accordance with the goals and methods of the Albanian terrorists and separatists."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At paragraph 1, we see a reference to defence plans?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please explain this to us. What kind of plans of defence are these within the SUP of Pristina?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: Within the secretariat, specifically within the police department within the secretariat, there were tasks of defence preparations for a police officer. Where there are bigger secretariats like the SUP of Pristina, then there would be two police officers involved in that, two police officers, from the police department, that is. They processed the work related to defence preparation plans because beforehand there was even a department for defence preparations at the level of bigger secretariats. These plans were adopted with a view to defending oneself from different kinds of dangers and threats.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You wouldn't know specifically what they pertained to. Did you ever take part in elaborating these defence plans?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: Well, no, I did not take part, but I think that this has to do with defence plans in terms of defending oneself from attacks by Albanian members of the KLA, terrorists. Defence from terrorist attacks, I think that is what this pertains to.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now the next page, 32.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In relation to the defence preparations, does this paragraph show who adopts instructions for this?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: "In accordance with the instructions of the ministry, forward reports on the number of members of the police reserve engaged," is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: It's the ministry that passed the instructions on the number of engaged members of the police reserve force.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]Now paragraph 4 on that same page.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: Do you have a question?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. Training of the reserve force, under whose jurisdiction is that?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: Well, the training of the reserve force is under the secretariat.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How were these work-plans made at SUP level?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: They were made, as I've already said, on the basis of the programme of work of the public security sector of the ministry. All lines of work made their own plans, then the OUPs made their own plans, and at the level of the analysis department of the secretariat, this was all brought together into the unified plan of the secretariat, which was then submitted to the ministry. As I've already mentioned, it was submitted in three copies. Again, in accordance with lines of work in the ministry, there was proper insight into these plans. Possible shortcomings and deficiencies were noted with a view to amending the plans until the final version was adopted. Once the final version was adopted of this annual plan of work, it was implemented during the course of the year, more specifically through monthly plans that were adopted towards the end of every month for the coming month, and they were also submitted to the analysis department in the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As for these work-plans, from the secretariat that you were a member of, did you send them to the MUP staff in Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: We did not send our annual work-plans to the MUP staff because there was no need to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What about monthly plans?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: Not them either.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now call up in e-court 6D269.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember this dispatch? You have it perhaps in your binder.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I do remember it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is this all about, briefly, please?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: This is a dispatch of the Ministry of the Interior sent to all organizational units of the ministry at the headquarters and to the secretariats on the 18th of February, 1999, setting certain priority tasks for the secretariats for the coming period and in relation to --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In relation to that work-plan for 1999, of the SUP of Pristina --

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- what does this dispatch represent?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: This is an order issuing dispatch from the ministry where certain priority tasks are supposed to be carried through in relation to the general situation in the country.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]I will now like to show 6D238.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just before moving from that, who is the main addressee of that document? Just every organizational unit?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the seat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can we go back, please, to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You heard the question of His Honour Judge Bonomy, so could you please tell us who the addressees are?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: The organizational units of the Ministry of the Interior of the public security sector at the headquarters; then to the SUPs from 1 through 33 to the respective chiefs; to the staff of the ministry in Pristina, to the head; then the border police stations, all of them; to the commander; then the state security sector here, meaning to the ministry headquarters, to the chief, for information purposes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. So now can we see 6D, or rather, I think it's time for our break, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. We have to have a break at this stage, Mr. Filic. We will be half an hour. Could you leave the courtroom, please, with the usher, and we will see you again at ten minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we, Mr. Filic?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]6D238, could we please have that document on e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You can find it in your own binder, too, 6D238. It is the third document I think.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember this dispatch?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: I remember the dispatch. It was sent by the Ministry of the Interior on the 24th of March, 1999, to organizational units of the RJB, all, at headquarters; then the SUPs; the MUP staff; and the border police stations, all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What kind of a dispatch is this, because we see that it refers to the one we saw a few moments ago as 6D269. So, in fact, is this a plan of the SUP?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: In fact, this is a more concrete dispatch. In relation to the previous one, it is being stated that the federal government on the 23rd of March declared an imminent threat of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] it says here in the transcript that I said this was a SUP plan and that the previous one -- well, what kind of a document is this, this dispatch, and in relation to the plan of the Pristina SUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is just for the transcript. Please go on.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: Organizational units are instructed to intensify the measures referred to in the previous dispatch on the 18th of February, since a state of imminent threat of war had been declared. So we are talking about the 24th of March, 1999. Operative work should be stepped-up on the part of all members of the ministry. There should be an intensification of patrol and all other activities that have to do with covering the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Just tell us whether this spells out the tasks in even more specific terms?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: Yes, in even more specific terms in comparison to the previous dispatch.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have 6D132, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is the second document in your binder. This is a dispatch dated the 25th of March, 1999.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: It can be stated that it's even more specific than the previous one, since the federal government had already declared a state of, war, and the most specific measures possible have been taken and orders issued to all units.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]6D688, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, is that number correct, 6D688?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that's what I have. Yes, 6D688.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Have you got it?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I don't think that document is in e-court. We have been trying to find it for some time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, was the witness have a hard copy?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, he does.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is it only in Serbian?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It has a translation as well, and we have it in the e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, it can't be found in e-court and -- sorry. It has now been released and is there. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Filic, what does this dispatch of the Ministry of the Interior dated the 5th of October, 1998, refer to?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: This is actually a document of the ministry; it is not a dispatch. It was signed by the minister. It was sent to all organizational units of the Ministry of the Interior; and in this document, the minister orders all the heads of the organizational units how to act in relation to relations with the media and providing proper information to the public, information pertaining to the work of the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How did you function as the spokesperson?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: When I was designated spokesperson, I cooperated, for the most part, with the then-media centre that was located at the Grand Hotel. That is where most of the foreign correspondents were based, too. With the chef de cabinet of the minister and also the information staff of the minister's office, I communicated about going out into the field. Usually, groups of journalists, foreigners, who were interested in going out into the field to tour a particular area contacted Mikim, or rather, Milorad Mihajlovic or his deputy Radovan Urosevic, and they presented their requests. Then these people would call me and ask me whether it was possible, in view of the security situation, to take them to a particular area. So after consultations with the minister's office, I would organize their safe travel to the mentioned areas. Usually, one of the two representatives of the media centre came along with me, Mihajlovic or Urosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So who did you receive your instructions from?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: From the head of the office of the minister of the interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: There was no -- hold on, Mr. Lukic, please. There was no interpretation of either the last question or the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. I just was warned about it, and I'll try to fix it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes. We need a live interpreter first, though.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Is it audible now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. We have it live, right. Can you repeat that question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Filic, it's not on the record. My question was: What about the MUP staff, did it have the right to organize press conferences?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: No, it did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You took journalists and reporters out into the field. Could you give us an example what they saw on these tours? We have seen on this footage the example of Junik. What else did they see?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: My first organized trip with reporters out into the field was after the beginning of anti-terrorist actions in Kosovo and Metohija in the area of Lapusnik village, which is on the route from Pristina to Pec, in the immediate vicinity of Komorane, where this main road had been besieged, cut off, for almost two month prior.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And who blocked this road before that?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: The KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Continue.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: I took them to the positions that had been engineered by the KLA. They were able to film and find out all they wanted to know. I gave them all the information I could; and after that, I took them to Kijevo village which was also in the same direction towards Pec. It had been besieged for two months before that. I showed them around together with the chief of police in that village. They could see on the way back that in the fields where the wheat was already ripe for harvesting, it was the end of July, there were large areas that are -- that were destroyed. Harvesting could not be done, and it was done by the KLA. I also took them to the Dulje mountain pass, which is on the route from Pristina towards Stimlje, Suva Reka, and Prizren. The road to Prizren had been under siege for almost two months. They could see all the fortifications and engineered positions of the KLA who had been holding this road under control. I also took them from Mitrovica via Srbica to Pec, the section of the road from Srbica to Rudnik, to a place called Zli Potok. It was a very peculiar section of the road where the KLA had cut the road off and held it under control and had dug out many kilometres of trenches along the road. All the reporters could see it with their own eyes, and their agencies, as far as I'm aware, have broadcast this information.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In view of the position you held, can you tell us what was the tendency, the trends, of terrorist attacks in the first half of 1998?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: In the first half of 1998, terrorist activities were stepped-up by the KLA. Even back in the end of 1997, they blocked part of the road from Srbica via Devic towards Klina. They held it for a long time; and then after the events this Likosane village, they escalated their activities even further.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When were these events in Likosane?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: End February 1998. Later, on in May, the town of Decani was blocked, railroad traffic from Kosovo Polje to Pec was blocked. All the roads I mentioned earlier were also under blockade towards Pec-Prizren, Mitrovica-Pec, and all the others. And, subsequently, specifically in the area of SUP Pristina, KLA stepped up its activities related to kidnappings of Serbs near the open pit mine Belacevac, the place from which the thermal power-station gets its coal. That's one of the first instance when nine Serb employees were kidnapped and taken away and nobody knows where. Just after that, in July, the town of Orahovac was attacked. There were fierce terrorist attacks one after the other. Kidnappings of Serbs in Retimlje village; 14 Serbs, members of one family, were abducted, and not even their remains have been found to date. And all this showed us that, without serious anti-terrorist action, there was no chance of normalising the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did they also proclaim their capital at the time?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: Yes. They proclaimed Malisevo as their capital. They started issuing some identification papers of their own making, licence plates marked KLA that were later found in a building where they were located in Malisevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I may have missed this, Mr. Filic, but what was the date of your appointment as the spokesperson?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] June 1998.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Beginning of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your opinion, why were anti-terrorist actions launched?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: Well, that was done for the purpose of liberating roads that had been completely blocked, and it was -- it had been impossible to use them. Traffic was impossible, and that also needed to be done to enable citizens to move around freely. I told you a moment ago which roads had been blocked, so the anti-terrorist actions were first geared at freeing those roads at the first stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Which event was a decisive factor in deciding to launch anti-terrorist actions?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: I think it was the 18th of July, 1998, when Orahovac was attacked.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And how long did these anti-terrorist actions last in 1998?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: Until the 25th of September, as far as I remember, end September.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know that a decision had been made at the state level to combat terrorism?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: I know. I haven't seen the decision, but I know that it existed in the form of a plan of anti-terrorist actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who were the main players to be involved in this struggle against terrorism?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: The Ministry of the Interior and the army of the FRY.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know if this plan was, indeed, realized in practice? Were anti-terrorist actions implemented according to the plan in 1998?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Whom did they target?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: Solely terrorists, members of the KLA who had brought the whole area in the situation I described earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were there any anti-terrorist actions in towns such as Pristina, Podujevo, Obilic, Kosovo Polje, Lipljan?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: In these towns in the area of SUP Pristina, there were no anti-terrorist actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What about some other towns, were there any anti-terrorist actions in other towns?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, there were some in Decani and in Orahovac when it was under siege and attacked by terrorists.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Why were there no anti-terrorist actions in some towns and they were launched in others?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: Because in that period in those towns, there were no terrorist attacks, unlike in Decani and in Orahovac. There was no need for anti-terrorist action there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you now about the agreement that opened the door to the Kosovo Verification Mission. After the completion of anti-terrorist actions, an agreement was made with the OSCE to establish the Kosovo Verification Mission. To the best of your knowledge, was this agreement with the OSCE observed and honoured by the MUP of the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: From what I know personally, I'm convinced that all the provisions of the agreement were honoured by the Ministry of the Interior. First and foremost, that applies to the check-points that existed before the agreement and those that were set up under the agreement and allowed to continue. So I believe the agreement was fully honoured as far as the activities of the MUP are concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What about the number of policemen, was it honoured in that respect?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: The number of policemen, the number of check-points, and everything else envisaged by the agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you have direct contact with members of the KVM?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: No, I did not. My position did not require it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you still have an opportunity to see that members of the KVM tolerated some prohibited conduct by the KLA?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Don't answer that question. It's such a leading question, Mr. Lukic, that the answer cannot assist us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can I rephrase it? May I rephrase it, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just a moment. Well, if you're wanting to lead evidence of prohibited conduct by the KLA, then there's no problem about that. But it's very difficult to see how you can rephrase the essence of the question, which is whether it was tolerated. Even that description makes it very difficult --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- to see how the witness could give evidence that would carry weight with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- as his own evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll move on. [Interpretation] May I call up in e-court P414.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And it's in your binder.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: Sorry, I didn't hear.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: I found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us what was the prevailing sentiment among the civilian population in December 1998?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: You mean in relation to this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In relation to the document and generally speaking.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: Generally speaking, the prevailing sentiment among the population in December 1998 was - I don't know how best to describe it - it was discontent. They were not satisfied with the security situation in the area of the secretariat, first of all, because individual members of the KLA continued their terrorist activities in some areas covered by the secretariat even with the presence of the KVM. It had been expected that with the arrival of the mission, security and safety would be restored instead of having the KLA continue with their terrorist activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who drafted the document before us?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: It was drafted by the Assembly Speaker of Podujevo municipality and the president of the Municipal Board of Podujevo municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was he reporting about in this letter?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: He is informing the president and all state officials in Serbia on the difficult security situation in the area of Podujevo municipality. He is explaining terrorist activities in certain areas around Podujevo and so on. They also asked for help and protection.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were any demonstrations there?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: Yes. There were dissatisfied Serb citizens who demonstrated in Podujevo. There were meetings at Podujevo municipality, at their building; and the chief of SUP sent me to Podujevo for a few days to see what it was all about and to assist the officials there to try and maintain the security levels. I spent a few days in the area of Podujevo, and I could see that on the road and at the entrance of Podujevo, as well as in the area of Glavnik village moving from Pristina to Podujevo to the left side of the road, KLA members had dug trenches some 4 to 500 metres to the side of the road and they used them to communicate. They often opened fire on the vehicles using that road as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At that time, did you know of any problems in the town of Pec?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: There were problems in Pec concerning a group of youngsters, boys who were killed in a bar. There were citizen demonstrations that followed expressing dissatisfaction with the security situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have P1580, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It is the last document in your binder. Were there any protests and the blocking of roads around Pristina; and if so, who organized it?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: This document is dated the 8th of January, 1999. It was drafted by the chief of SUP of Pristina, informing the ministry of the events around Pristina. We can see that there were protests on several roads, protests staged by Serbs, because of the incidents that took place at the open-pit mine at Belacevac where a guard was killed, a certain Delic from Laplje Selo, Laplje village.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you have anything to do with the calming down of the situation?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: No, not directly, but I know that measures were taken to decrease tensions, and at some point the crowd dispersed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please focus on Pristina SUP next. Explain in brief the way Pristina SUP was organized, first along the professional lines, together along with the number of personnel.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: The SUP in Pristina was one of the bigger secretariats, or rather, the biggest secretariat in Kosovo and Metohija, and at the level of bigger secretariats in the territory of the Republic of Serbia. It was organized similar to the SUPs of Nis, Kragujevac, and Novi Sad. The organizational structure, professionally-wise, was such that we had nine departments within the secretariat. Territorially speaking, there were five OUPs which fell under that SUP. There was a department of the police, of the crime police, of the traffic police; the department in charge of the borders, aliens, and travel documents; the department of the fire brigade, or the fire-fighting police, as a matter of fact; then the communications department; the analysis department; and common affairs department; the last was the legal department. The OUPs which fell under the SUP of Pristina were Podujevo, Lipljan, Glogovac, Kosovo Polje, and Obilic, with the police stations in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I forgot to ask you about staff composition.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: Staff appointments within the secretariat was in accordance with the organizational structure --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please give us the names.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: All those in leading positions were qualified in keeping with the rules on systemization of job posts. Bosko Petric was the chief of SUP; I was his deputy; the chief of the police department was Zarko Brakovic; chief of the crime police department was Dragan Pavlovic or Dragoslav; chief of the traffic police department was Miladin Vujosevic; chief of the border department in charge of aliens and travel documents as well was Slobodan Markovic; chief of the communications department, Milos Deretic; chief of the fire brigade was Miodrag Martinovic; chief of the joint or common affairs department was Milorad Rajicic. Chief of the analysis and IT department was Negica Grkovic; and in the administrative affairs department, it was Gordana Cerovic; chiefs of OUPs in Lipljan, it was Nikola Ilic; in Podujevo, Milan Radulovic; in Kosovo Polje, Dragan Miric; in Obilic, Bozidar Spasic; and in Glogovac, Damjanac Petar who testified here yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please explain what the authority of the SUP in Pristina was.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: It was supposed to execute all tasks assigned to it according to the Law on Internal Affairs within its territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the territory meaning what sector?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: The sector of public security.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did Pristina SUP have an obligation to communicate with the state security sector, the Army of Yugoslavia, various prosecutor's offices, courts, inspections, citizens, the chief of the district, presidents of municipalities, and other officials?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: The Pristina SUP was supposed to cooperate with all of those, and so we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were there border police stations within the Pristina SUP territory?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: There was one at the Pristina airport.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who issued orders to the police station at the airport?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: As well as any other border police station, they received their orders from their professional administration within the ministry in charge of the border and aliens.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Where is that administration located?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: It is a part of the Ministry of the Interior in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who is the SUP's chief's superior?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: His superior was the head of the public security sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who appoints and replaces people and down to what level within the secretariat?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: Within the secretariat, appointment to certain positions, meaning leadership positions, when we're talking about the uniformed part of the police and going down as far as the police station commander, and with the civilian part of the police, it goes as low as the chiefs of independent sectors. Such appointments are made by the chief of the public security sector. For lower-ranking positions, such appointments are made by the SUP chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Concerning disciplinary measures, can you explain the procedure before the war, before the 8th of April, 1998?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: For any infractions in line of duty, qualified as minor breaches of work duty, measures are taken by the chief of SUP, as follows: The immediate superior of the employee who committed an infraction opens a file, takes the employee's statement, and includes other evidence. It is then forwarded to the chief of SUP who pronounces an appropriate disciplinary measure. For less serious infractions, those could include fines or warnings. Employees could appeal that decision to the disciplinary court of the secretariat. When we talk about more serious infractions, the disciplinary procedure was conducted before the disciplinary court. Such proceedings, as with the immediate -- as in the previous cases, the immediate superior opens and file and writes a disciplinary report. The file then goes to the chief of SUP; and should the chief establish that there was an infraction, a request for disciplinary proceedings is created and then forwarded to the disciplinary court, which is in charge of any further proceedings. The measures should be those of fining, demoting a person to a lower rank of duty for a year or two, or terminating their employment. The employee concerned could appeal the decision of the court of the secretariat with the appeals court of the ministry, which would be the second instance.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When the war began on the 8th of April, 1999, were there any changes in terms of procedure?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: When the war began and when the decree on the work of the ministry in wartime conditions was issued with the date you mentioned, the 8th of April, there were changes concerning more serious infractions or violations of work duty. As of that date, the chief of the secretariat could issue disciplinary measures to his employees for serious violations. I believe the intention was to shorten the procedure in wartime conditions. As for any proceedings before disciplinary courts, it takes time and this was considered to be a more efficient way of dealing with disciplinary violations. Employees could again appeal to the higher disciplinary court with the ministry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just a moment, Mr. Lukic. Mr. Filic, is what happened to Mr. Damjanac an example of the operation of this system?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know what you have in mind, Your Honour. What happened?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, he was removed, was he not, from his OUP?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I wasn't in Pristina on the 1st of May when he was replaced. I don't know how that was viewed or how it can be explained.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, he told us he was demoted.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He used to be chief of OUP, and they demoted him down to an -- to the level of an operative worker.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And that was something that, because of the wartime conditions, the chief of the SUP would have power to do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Concerning Damjanac, that was not a part of any disciplinary procedure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I see. Thank you. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did the chief of SUP have the authority and right to transfer employees to different jobs?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: Yes, for those under the level that I already talked about for which decisions have to be made by the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to ask you the following: What were disciplinary proceedings like if an infraction was committed by a member of the PJP, rather, special police units?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC
utterances.text: Members of the PJPs had the same rule applies to them; but if they were outside the area of their secretariat, if they were sent to a different area, and if they committed the breach there, then the immediate superior would make up a case file, then that would be sent to the original secretariat, and that is where the proceedings would be initiated.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So -- it would be a leading question. Never mind. I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Who would be the superior who would compile the file or open the file for a PJP person working in a different secretariat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The commander of the PJP unit would be such an officer, for example.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. Lukic, can you find a suitable place to interrupt.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I can interrupt right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Filic, we have to bring our proceedings for the day to an end because another case is in this courtroom this afternoon and we can't continue; that means that you have to return on Monday to complete your evidence. Between now and then, it is vital that you should have no communication with any person at all, it doesn't matter who that person is, about the evidence in this case, any aspect of that evidence. There are plenty other things to apply your mind to over the weekend, forget about this case, do not discuss the evidence in the case, but return here at 9.00 on Monday morning. Now, could you please leave the courtroom with the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And we adjourn now until 9.00 on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
